description:
The messages table (after migration 0012) has no user_id column. Per-user DEK encryption of message content requires knowing which user owns each message, so we know which DEK to use. Re-add user_id.

## Background
  Migration 0012 dropped user_id from messages to make the table 'shared'.
  For v1 single-user this was harmless (all messages belong to user 1).
  For encryption and multi-user readiness, we need user_id back.

## Migration

  ALTER TABLE messages ADD COLUMN user_id BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1
      REFERENCES users(id);
  CREATE INDEX idx_messages_user ON messages (user_id);

  Existing rows get user_id = 1 (the singleton user in v1 deployments).
  The DEFAULT 1 is a migration convenience only; application code must
  always supply the correct user_id explicitly.

## Code changes
  All INSERT paths into messages must supply user_id from the authenticated
  caller context. Search for INSERT INTO messages in:
    - crates/mail/src/smtp/ (inbound delivery path)
    - crates/mail/src/email/ (JMAP Email/set, Email/import)
  Each must be updated to pass the user_id.

## Acceptance
  - Migration runs on both SQLite and Postgres
  - All INSERT paths supply an explicit user_id (no reliance on DEFAULT 1 at runtime)
  - Existing tests pass (they use user_id = 1 which matches DEFAULT 1 for existing rows)
title: Add user_id to messages table (prerequisite for per-user DEK on email)
